historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue CAGR (3yr 3.2%, 5yr 3.9%) tempered by FY26's +0.2% and the AGM 18-week FY27 update of +3.5% (+2.8% ex-tobacco)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 16.7% vs revenue 3.2% and EPS -1.8%: the divergence is the $351.9m FY24 equity raise for Superior Foods (ShareIssuanceProceeds FY2024), not retained earnings; equity CAGR is rejected as the growth anchor. Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR of 27.7% is off the FY23 working-capital trough ($93.8m) and the 5yr figure of -5.5% is off the FY21 COVID-inflated peak ($259.2m); neither is a trend, the through-cycle owner-FCF level is ~$180-220m.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = FreeCashFlow - StockBasedComp - LeasePrincipalPaid (FY20 onward, post IFRS-16; pre-FY20 leases were already in operating cash flow): FY21 259.2, FY22 153.5, FY23 93.8, FY24 188.5, FY25 221.4, FY26 195.6. The FY26 last_fcf of 179.8 additionally nets the lease financing component and sublease receipts, which the CSV does not carry by year. CAGRs are FY2023->FY2026 (3yr) and FY2021->FY2026 (5yr), fiscal years ending 30 April.

scenario_narratives.base: Metcash remains Australia's fourth grocery force with a stable ~7-10% independent share, Liquor keeps taking share (32.3% and rising), and Hardware recovers slowly from three years of EBIT decline. Sales grow ~3% organically; the EBITDA margin edges from 4.39% to 4.50% as TTHG duplication is removed and Program Horizon (complete FY27) lowers cost-to-serve; capex normalises from the Horizon peak. Net leases stay 1.15% of sales, cash tax 29%, and the terminal multiple is held at today's ~15x unlevered owner FCF, so no re-rating is assumed. Bolt-on retail M&A is excluded.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Hardware cycle turns with housing/renovation activity and the TTHG merger delivers mid-cycle margins; Foodservice & Convenience, Sorted (~30% of Group revenue) and LocalEyes retail media compound higher-margin revenue; the mandatory Food and Grocery Code and excessive-pricing prohibition on Coles/Woolworths lift independents' relative standing; Horizon delivers its cost benefits. Sales grow 4-4.5% for five years and the EBITDA margin reaches 4.85%; terminal 16x at 2.75% growth.
scenario_narratives.bear: The duopoly and ALDI grind share and price, a large Multiple Store Owner vertically integrates or switches supplier, Hardware never leaves its trough, illicit tobacco keeps eroding a high-margin category, and Horizon overruns while the lease book (already $1.2bn gross) grows faster than sales. Sales stall at ~1% nominal, the EBITDA margin sags to 4.0%, capex stays elevated and the market pays only 12x terminal FCF. No solvency issue: net debt / EBITDA stays inside the 1.0-1.75x target band, so the bear is a margin and multiple case, not a going-concern case.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the unlevered owner cash flow of a thin-margin, defensive wholesale distributor at an AUD WACC, with leases charged once as an operating cost (net of the back-to-back subleases) and excluded from net debt, the Total Tools put liabilities and NCI deducted once in the bridge, SBC expensed (immaterial at 0.02% of sales) and the share count held flat. The terminal multiple is capped at the multiple the stock trades on today, so the valuation depends on the sustainability of a ~4.4-4.5% EBITDA margin and ~3% growth, not on a re-rating. Risk is expressed through the bear/bull flows and a 25/50/25 weighting, not through per-scenario discount rates.
key_risks_to_valuation: Loss or vertical integration of a large Multiple Store Owner (Ritchies, Romeo Retail Group, Drakes) would remove Food volume the base case assumes is stable
Hardware & Tools has had three years of EBIT decline; the base assumes only a slow recovery, but a deeper housing downturn takes the margin path toward the bear case
Net lease cash (1.15% of sales) is a larger charge than SBC or capex; if store leases grow faster than sales or sublessee retailers default on back-to-back leases, the margin assumption breaks
Program Horizon (cumulative $286.7m) and TTHG integration: overruns or non-delivery of cost-to-serve benefits push the base margin path down
Illicit tobacco and excise policy: legal tobacco sales are down 52% since FY21; the FY27 rebound (+11.7% in the 18-week update) depends on enforcement
Bolt-on M&A is excluded from the flows; if management keeps deploying $70-400m a year at low returns, the modelled organic value overstates what shareholders receive
Terminal multiple: the base 15x cap equals today's multiple; a permanent de-rating of ASX grocery/wholesale to 12x is the bear terminal and costs ~$0.60/share

inputs.sbc_source: MTS.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt:3961 share-based payments expense $3.0m (FY25 $3.1m); no net-share-settlement taxes disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0); statement of changes in equity shows $0.5m settled in cash
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,099.7m ordinary shares on issue at 30 April 2026 (Annual FY2026 note 5.4) plus the 5.1m dilutive effect of performance rights from the FY26 diluted-EPS note (line 4163). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would double-charge it. The DRP is suspended from the FY26 final dividend, so no further DRP issuance is assumed. Buyback cash is 0 in FY23-FY26 (the last off-market buyback was $200.4m in FY22); the flat count is a modelling convention that a $3m/yr SBC charge easily funds.
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-built. Risk-free 4.3% (10-year ACGB, Sep-2026), ERP 5.5%, beta 0.85 (defensive grocery wholesale with a cyclical Hardware pillar) gives a ~9.0% cost of equity; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.6% (BBSW + syndicated margin; $495m swapped at 4.0% pre-margin) is ~3.9% after 30% tax; ex-lease capital structure ~82% equity / 18% debt at the current market cap gives ~8.1%, rounded to 8.0%. One WACC across all three scenarios; risk is carried in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B): leases as operating cost. The net lease cash charge is deducted inside adjusted EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path, and lease liabilities ($1,217.2m at 30 April 2026) are EXCLUDED from net debt. FY26 net lease cash = $184.2m principal (financing) + $55.1m net financing component (operating) - $39.3m sublease receipts (investing) = $200.0m = 1.15% of revenue (Annual FY2026 cash flow statement lines 3733-3746). Metcash is a large sublessor to its independent retailers on back-to-back terms, so the gross lease liability overstates the economic obligation; the net charge is the right cost. D&A for cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation: $258.0m total less $154.1m ROU = $103.9m = 0.60% of revenue (line 3963-3967). Net debt of $616.6m matches the company's own definition, which also excludes leases.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (NCI profit share only $1.7m in FY26), so the NCI book value of $10.7m is deducted once in the equity bridge, together with the $96.4m Total Tools / Hardware JV put option liabilities (FY26 funds-employed table, line 504), which are the contracted cost of buying out the remaining JV partners. Any overlap between the two is under $0.01/share.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical'), with owner-fcf-adaptations (a1) AUD WACC, (b) lease treatment B, (c) NCI charged once in the bridge, (e) SBC-near-zero so house and street coincide (band_position null), (f) risk charged once. Metcash earns a thin wholesale margin on ~$17.4bn of sales to independent Food, Liquor and Hardware retailers; value is a stream of cash flow, so the FCF engine applies. last_fcf is owner FCF on a lease-consistent basis: reported FCF 382.8 (OCF 558.0 - capex 175.2) less SBC 3.0 less net lease cash 200.0 = 179.8; it is a levered anchor only, the engine projects unlevered flows from components. Interest income ($2.0m) is not stripped because the company is a net borrower. FY0 component check: EBITDA 761.7 - lease 200.0 - SBC 3.0 - D&A ex-ROU 103.9 = 454.8 ex-lease EBIT, which ties to reported underlying EBIT 503.7 less the 55.1 lease financing component (448.6) within the ROU-depreciation-vs-principal timing gap; NOPAT at 29% + D&A - capex = ~252 unlevered owner FCF, and less after-tax bank interest (~46) plus the FY26 working-capital release (27.4) reconciles to the 179.8 levered figure. Bolt-on acquisitions ($68.9m FY26, $403.8m FY25 incl. Superior Foods) are outside both the flows and the growth path: the growth rates are organic, and retail M&A is a bull-case lever, not a base assumption. Working capital: a distributor with receivables + inventory > payables (NWC $429.3m = 2.5% of revenue), so wc_capture is NEGATIVE (growth consumes cash). Terminal cap 15x in base equals today's EV / FY26 unlevered owner FCF (~15x), so no multiple expansion is assumed.

bear.narrative: Woolworths/Coles/ALDI scale pressure and a large MSO (Ritchies, Romeo, Drakes-type) loss hold sales to ~1% nominal, Hardware stays in its trough, illicit tobacco keeps eroding the category, Horizon overruns and the lease base grows faster than sales: EBITDA margin sags to 4.0% and the terminal multiple compresses to 12x.

base.narrative: Organic sales growth of ~3% (grocery inflation plus Liquor share gains and a modest Hardware recovery, no bolt-on M&A), EBITDA margin drifting from 4.39% to 4.50% as TTHG duplication costs come out and Program Horizon lowers cost-to-serve, capex normalising from the Horizon peak of 1.0% of sales to 0.75%, and D&A ex-ROU rising as Horizon software amortises.

bull.narrative: Hardware cycle turns (Total Tools high-single-digit growth sustained, TTHG synergies return Hardware to mid-cycle margins), Foodservice & Convenience and Sorted keep compounding, LocalEyes retail media adds a high-margin stream, the mandatory Grocery Code blunts the majors, and Horizon delivers its cost-to-serve benefits: EBITDA margin reaches 4.85%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35. Bear raised to 25% because underlying profit has fallen two years running (FY25 -2.4%, FY26 -2.4%) while net debt has risen from $251.9m to $616.6m on acquisitions, MSO customer concentration is a real single-point risk in Food, and the duopoly's structural scale advantage caps margin. Bull cut to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once: a Hardware cycle turn, TTHG and Horizon benefit realisation, and the Grocery Code actually shifting share. No going-concern or covenant stress (leverage inside the 1.0-1.75x band, $967m undrawn), so the bear is not weighted higher than 25%.
probability_weighted.band_note: SBC is 0.02% of sales, so the house and street bases coincide (street IV is 6c above house); the accounting-regime band collapses to a point and band_position is not meaningful. Reported as null, not as a degenerate percentage.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
